title: Why an equation is like a balance
keywords: do the same to both sides
examples: Why is an equation like a balance?
Why do you do the same thing to both sides?

explain.say: Look at the balance. On the left are two mystery boxes called x, and a 1. On the right is a 9. The scale is level, so both sides weigh the same. This picture is the equation 2x plus 1 equals 9.

explain.say: Look at the 9 on the right. The equals sign means level, just like this scale. If you take something off one side only, it tips. So whatever you do, you must do it to both sides. Makes sense?

right.ask: Why must both sides stay balanced?

explain.say: Let us take 1 off both sides. Now two x boxes balance 8. See? Still level! That is the equation 2x equals 8.
Two boxes weigh 8, so cut both sides in half. One x box balances 4. So x is 4! Look at the x box on the left.

explain.say: Brilliant, you solved it! Check: 2 times 4 plus 1 is 9. Yes! Wow: the word algebra comes from al-jabr, an Arabic word for restoring balance, from a book written in Baghdad about 1,200 years ago. Challenge: solve 3x plus 2 equals 11.

faq.q: What does x stand for on the balance?
faq.a: x is a mystery number, like a box whose weight you do not know yet. Solving the equation means finding its weight. Here x is 4.
asks: What is x in an equation?

faq.q: Why must both sides stay balanced?
faq.a: The equals sign says both sides are worth the same. If you change only one side, they are no longer equal, like a scale tipping.
asks: Why do you do the same thing to both sides?

faq.a: To get the x boxes alone. Taking 1 from both sides keeps the balance level and leaves 2x equals 8.
asks: How do you get x on its own?

faq.q: How do you solve 3x plus 2 equals 11?
faq.a: Take 2 from both sides to get 3x equals 9. Then divide both sides by 3. x is 3.

faq.q: How do you check your answer?
faq.a: Put your number back into the equation. If x is 4, then 2 times 4 plus 1 is 9, so it is right.
asks: How do I know my answer is correct?

facts: The word algebra comes from al-jabr in the title of a book by al-Khwarizmi, written in Baghdad in the 800s CE.
Al-jabr means restoring or completing, as when you move terms to keep an equation balanced.

quiz.why: Take 3 from both sides to get 2x equals 8. Halve both sides: x is 4.

wrong.1: 7 forgets to take away the 3 first, or halves the wrong number.
wrong.2: 8 is 2x, not x. You still need to halve it.

quiz.say: In 5x equals 20, what do you do to both sides?
quiz.why: 5x means 5 times x, so dividing both sides by 5 gives x equals 4.

wrong.1: Taking away 5 gives 5x minus 5, which does not get x alone.
wrong.2: Adding 5 makes it harder, not easier.
